statements.label: supported
statements.text: Particular TE families and subfamilies have given rise to 3D chromatin structures specific to individual mammalian lineages.
statements.evidence: We show that specific families and subfamilies of TEs have contributed to lineage-specific 3D chromatin structures across mammalian species.
statements.note: The abstract reports specific TE families and subfamilies produced lineage-specific 3D chromatin structures across mammals.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: TE-derived CTCF binding sites are more common in primate genomes than in rodent genomes.
statements.evidence: including the multifarious master protein, CTCF, which shapes the 3D genome by creating loops, domains, compartment borders, and RNA-DNA interactions.
statements.note: The abstract notes TEs carry CTCF binding sites but never compares their abundance between primate and rodent genomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study quantified how transposable elements give rise to loops and domain-border differences across multiple cell types and species using several 3D genome mapping technologies.
statements.evidence: we explore the widespread contribution of TEs to mammalian 3D genomes by quantifying the extent to which they give rise to loops and domain border differences across various cell types and species using several 3D genome mapping technologies.
statements.note: The abstract reports quantifying TE contributions to loops and domain-border differences across cell types and species with several 3D mapping technologies.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting a candidate transposable element with CRISPR-Cas9 disrupted the 3D chromatin structure specific to a species.
statements.evidence: An experimental validation of our analytical findings using CRISPR-Cas9 to delete a candidate TE resulted in disruption of species-specific 3D chromatin structure.
statements.note: The abstract reports CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of a candidate TE disrupted species-specific 3D chromatin structure.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of replicated retrotransposon DNA, a larger fraction (90%) persisted as extrachromosomal circular DNA than the fraction (10%) that produced new insertions.
statements.evidence: found that 10% of them achieve new insertions, whereas 90% exist as extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA)
statements.note: The study found 90% of replicated retrotransposon DNA remained as eccDNA, versus 10% that produced new insertions.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Retrotransposon second-strand synthesis by alt-EJ proceeds more efficiently in germline cells than in somatic cells.
statements.evidence: alt-EJ drives the second-strand synthesis of the long terminal repeat retrotransposon DNA through a circularization process
statements.note: The abstract describes alt-EJ-driven second-strand synthesis but makes no comparison between germline and somatic cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Retrotransposons co-opt the host's alternative end-joining repair pathway, via a circularization step, to build the second strand of their DNA.
statements.evidence: retrotransposons hijack the alternative end-joining (alt-EJ) DNA repair process of the host for a circularization step to synthesize their second-strand DNA.
statements.note: The abstract reports retrotransposons hijack host alt-EJ repair, through circularization, to synthesize their second-strand DNA.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genetic screens pinpointed alt-EJ components as required for retrotransposons to replicate.
statements.evidence: further genetic screens identified factors from alt-EJ as essential for retrotransposon replication.
statements.note: The study's genetic screens identified alt-EJ factors as essential for retrotransposon replication.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The regulatory endogenous retrovirus families identified lie close to genes showing higher expression in trophoblast.
statements.evidence: we identified multiple endogenous retrovirus families with regulatory potential that lie close to genes with preferential expression in trophoblast.
statements.note: The abstract reports regulatory ERV families lying close to genes preferentially, more highly, expressed in trophoblast.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genetic editing showed several of these elements act as transcriptional enhancers for placental genes including CSF1R and PSG5.
statements.evidence: we demonstrate that several elements act as transcriptional enhancers of important placental genes, such as CSF1R and PSG5.
statements.note: The abstract reports genetic editing confirmed several elements act as enhancers of placental genes such as CSF1R and PSG5.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: An LTR10A element was found to control ENG expression and thereby the secretion of soluble endoglin, relevant to preeclampsia.
statements.evidence: We also identify an LTR10A element that regulates ENG expression, affecting secretion of soluble endoglin, with potential implications for preeclampsia.
statements.note: The abstract reports an LTR10A element regulating ENG and affecting soluble-endoglin secretion, with possible preeclampsia relevance.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The primate-specific ERV enhancers arose more recently than the placental genes they regulate.
statements.evidence: These largely primate-specific elements are associated with inter-species gene expression differences and are bound by transcription factors with key roles in placental development.
statements.note: The abstract calls the elements primate-specific but never compares their evolutionary age with that of the regulated genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: L1 ORF2p nicks target DNA more efficiently than the endonucleases encoded by other retrotransposons.
statements.evidence: L1 spreads through a mechanism termed target-primed reverse transcription, in which the encoded enzyme (ORF2p) nicks the target DNA to prime reverse transcription of its own or non-self RNAs
statements.note: The abstract describes ORF2p nicking target DNA but never compares its efficiency with endonucleases of other retrotransposons.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: L1 ORF2p uses upstream single-stranded DNA to place the adjacent duplex in its endonuclease active site, nicking the longer DNA strand.
statements.evidence: L1 ORF2p relies on upstream single-stranded DNA to position the adjacent duplex in the endonuclease active site for nicking of the longer DNA strand
statements.note: The abstract states ORF2p uses upstream single-stranded DNA to position the duplex for nicking the longer DNA strand.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A sequence-specific polyadenosine tract in the template RNA is recognized by five separate domains of the enzyme.
statements.evidence: The template polyadenosine tract is recognized in a sequence-specific manner by five distinct domains.
statements.note: The abstract reports the template poly(A) tract is recognized by five distinct domains.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The researchers purified intact L1 ORF2p and rebuilt target-primed reverse transcription in vitro with template RNA and target-site DNA.
statements.evidence: we purified full-length L1 ORF2p and biochemically reconstituted robust target-primed reverse transcription with template RNA and target-site DNA.
statements.note: The abstract reports purifying full-length ORF2p and reconstituting target-primed reverse transcription with template RNA and target DNA.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A genome-wide reporter assay flagged transposable elements with functional enhancer activity in two endoderm-derived cancers, colorectal and liver.
statements.evidence: we utilize unbiased massively parallel reporter assay data using a whole human genome library to identify TEs with functional enhancer activity in two human cancer types of endodermal lineage, colorectal and liver cancers.
statements.note: The abstract reports a genome-wide MPRA identified TEs with enhancer activity in colorectal and liver cancers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Distinct TE subfamilies serve as tissue-specific enhancers, MER11 elements in colon cancer and LTR12 elements in liver cancer.
statements.evidence: we identify distinct TE subfamilies that function as tissue-specific enhancers, namely MER11- and LTR12-elements in colon and liver cancers, respectively.
statements.note: The abstract reports MER11 elements act as enhancers in colon cancer and LTR12 elements in liver cancer.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The TE enhancers identified carry hallmarks of active enhancers, such as epigenetic marks and transcription-factor binding.
statements.evidence: the identified TE enhancers are characterized by genomic features associated with active enhancers, such as epigenetic marks and TF binding.
statements.note: The abstract states the identified TE enhancers show active-enhancer features like epigenetic marks and TF binding.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Silencing LINC01876 by CRISPR interference reduced the size of cerebral organoids and drove neural progenitors to differentiate prematurely.

statements.note: The abstract reports CRISPRi silencing of LINC01876 reduced cerebral-organoid size and caused premature neural-progenitor differentiation.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.note: The abstract links L1 transcripts to human-brain diversification but makes no comparison of cognitive contribution across primates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: L1 elements give rise to hundreds of developmentally regulated, cell-type-specific transcripts, many co-opted as chimeric transcripts or regulatory RNAs.

statements.note: The abstract reports L1s generate hundreds of developmentally regulated, cell-type-specific transcripts, many used as chimeric or regulatory RNAs.

statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported

statements.label: supported
